title: the bench host's CI runner, made safe for a public repository
note: basis 'shown' means shown by the tree or the card's own tests; nothing was installed or run on the bench host: every host-side claim is the walk's to show.

findings.claim: a one-job runner needs a fresh registration per job, and a registration token lasts about an hour, so the host holds a fine-grained token of the owner's account (this repository only, Administration: write, 30-day expiry: the owner's choice of 2026-11-24); it can change the repository's settings: since the review of #1448 (F2) only the units' root steps read it (mint before a job, cleanup after) and the jobs' user never can
findings.fix: the owner's choice: keep the token's expiry short and revoke it with the remove step (the page says so), or rule another credential

findings.claim: every profile has a read-only root, every capability dropped and no fuse or tun device (the review of #1448, F5); the engine and GPU profiles keep SETUID and SETGID and cannot set no-new-privileges, because the nested rootless engine maps its user namespace with the set-id helpers; those profiles run on trains and the owner's runs only

ruled 2026-11-24: the GPU jobs get the host's weights folder read-only at /weights (the version check uses the pinned hashes; no download); the GPU suites still need a model server started on the CI cards from those weights, which no step does yet, so the gpu-suites and full-set jobs report the gpu stage as not started until that step is built

no make target runs the real-model rehearsal (deploy/install.sh --rehearsal-real-servers, H-89) in CI: it needs pinned weights and the engine probe on the job's own card; the bench workflow's rehearse-box job runs the box rehearsal with the stand-ins, and the real-model rehearsal is not wired

the egress allow-list names hosts exactly (no storage wildcard, no user-content wildcard, and no upload host the proxy can tell from a download host: it sees the name only, so a host that takes both under one name is reachable for both), and jobs have no name service; whether the list is enough for every job is known only from the first runs (the proxy logs each refused host by name)

a job can read its own runner's credentials (the one-job configuration, now a file the entry point deletes after unpacking it, the review's F9); they end with that job and its container, and no job sees another's
the install page is a part of RUNBOOK section 13 (docs/runbook/13-bench-ci-runner.md), as the integrator gives section numbers; a number of its own needs the integrator's row

the host's gate (the review of #1448, F1) rests on the runner handing its job-started hook the GITHUB_* variables and the event payload as the code host sent them; the tests feed the gate stand-ins for both, and that the runner does so is shown only by the walk's first jobs

since the review of #1448 (F5) a lane push gets the CPU jobs only (unit shards, integration); the GPU suites, full-set and the box rehearsal need the engine or GPU profile and run on trains and the owner's runs only, which is less than the owner's ruling of 2026-11-24 item 8 (every lane PR gets the GPU suites)

H-105b's GPU box rehearsal cannot take the first-run step on a rehearsal box: deploy/box-install.sh refuses --rehearsal with --firstrun (H-94 (3)); the job records the TPM, the GPU record, the read-only weights folder and its own engine, and says NOT RUN for the install under a real init, the first-run step and the unit start until that is ruled, and for the serving step until it is built

the runner did not install on the bench host (the walk's first install at 1fc6579e): a scratch folder beside the user's home was refused, the install ended with an unbound variable after 'installed', the units sent the engine to root's runtime folder (a system unit's %U is 0), the proxy's engine did not see its network (reproduced on the distribution's 4.9.3 and netavark 1.4: without /var/lib/cni the engine hides /var/lib, the user's home, while it sets up a rootless network), and install.sh had no execute bit; each is fixed and held by a test that runs the step, and none is shown on the host until the walk's real-host test (tools/bench_ci/host_test.sh) is clean
findings.fix: the walk runs tools/bench_ci/host_test.sh on the bench host and posts its report on the pull request; #1466 rides only after that run is clean

findings.claim: remove deleted, as root, whatever the settings named as scratch, including a folder install had refused as another owner's, and the host test ran remove after a failed install (OCR 1466-2); remove now deletes only what install recorded that it made (a root-only record written before each thing, whole), and the host test never runs remove after a failed install
